rationale: Unset admits fixed FP64 J/K/range-K anchors at 192 or more AOs for relaxed application-budget Fast WB97M-V restricted exact-Direct cold nonlocal outer solves, without a fixed upper AO limit. Shared budget-Fock admission also has no fixed AO or atom-count ceiling; native dimensions, actual resources and all other scientific conditions remain checked. Explicit 1 opts in smaller scientifically eligible owners; 0 disables. Provisional operators act on total current-minus-anchor density; full targets refresh strict anchors and nonlinear XC/VV10 retain total density. Unsupported domains, warm solves and optional device-allocation failure preserve the incumbent path. Five FP64 matrices and one scalar are charged, then retired at a pressured force handoff without revoking D/W/XC or the final token; later solves use ordinary Fast. Numerical acceptance thresholds are unchanged. Historical measurements do not qualify every newly admitted larger shape. Separately, explicit 1 admits strict-FP64 one-spin exact full/range Direct VV10 owners without a resource ledger and with chunk width one; strict unset/0 and AUTO-only owners retain the incumbent path. This strict domain remains opt-in, not part of the already-default Fast policy. Checkpoint execution identity includes the selector; existing research measurements are not exact-PR-source qualification.
revisit_condition: Require profitable complete-endpoint evidence before lowering the 192-AO automatic floor: retained water-12 observations are adverse. Removing count ceilings is not a new large-size accuracy or speed qualification. Record independent large-system energy/force gates and actual work/resource failures separately. Qualify other models, precision, spin, DF, warm, chunk or public resource-ledger anchor domains independently; preserve strict full-target audits, explicit rollback and force-phase optional-memory fallback. Require source-bound complete endpoints and independent scientific/work/resource gates before any strict default promotion; do not transfer combined-research timings to the isolated strict source.
